# Command line reference

`--help` output of every `naga` command, captured live so it cannot drift from the real argument parsers. `python -m nagasim` is the same program.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`naga examples`](#naga-examples) | list the models that ship in the package |
| [`naga run`](#naga-run) | run a model headless |
| [`naga scenarios`](#naga-scenarios) | run named scenarios headless and compare them |
| [`naga invest`](#naga-invest) | payback, NPV and ROI of each scenario against a baseline |
| [`naga fit`](#naga-fit) | fit an input distribution to CSV data |
| [`naga doe`](#naga-doe) | design of experiments over model parameters |
| [`naga optimize`](#naga-optimize) | search model parameters for the best KPI within a replication budget |
| [`naga policy-eval`](#naga-policy-eval) | evaluate a controller against a Policy-mode DECIDE |
| [`naga schema`](#naga-schema) | JSON Schema of the model file format |
| [`naga validate`](#naga-validate) | structured validation problems, exit 1 on errors |
| [`naga fmt`](#naga-fmt) | rewrite model files in their shortest canonical form |
| [`naga export`](#naga-export) | write a model as Python code that builds it (nagasim.build) |
| [`naga diff`](#naga-diff) | semantic diff of two model files by record identity |
| [`naga merge`](#naga-merge) | three-way merge of model files by record identity |
| [`naga check`](#naga-check) | run a model's assertions and reality checks |
| [`naga ci-template`](#naga-ci-template) | print a GitHub Actions workflow running 'naga check' |
| [`naga generate`](#naga-generate) | build a model from Stations/Products/Routings tables |
| [`naga discover`](#naga-discover) | draft a model from an event log (CSV or XES), with a report of what it assumed |
| [`naga sdimport`](#naga-sdimport) | translate an XMILE/Vensim file into a model JSON |
| [`naga viewer`](#naga-viewer) | one HTML file in which the engine re-runs a model in a browser |
| [`naga bind`](#naga-bind) | resolve a model's data bindings and show what each one read |
| [`naga watch`](#naga-watch) | print what a model's live data sources send, as it arrives |
| [`naga state`](#naga-state) | take a model's state from a run or from a plant, and check one before a start |
| [`naga plant`](#naga-plant) | map what a plant sends into an observed timeline: check, replay a log, watch |
| [`naga twin`](#naga-twin) | an operational twin: monitor a plant, forecast from its state, compare, report |
| [`naga calibrate`](#naga-calibrate) | fit model parameters to observed KPIs |
| [`naga forecast`](#naga-forecast) | short-horizon forecast with prediction bands |
| [`naga plan`](#naga-plan) | deterministic plan, optional CP-SAT proposal and risk |
| [`naga loops`](#naga-loops) | loop dominance (Loops That Matter) of an SD model |
| [`naga mcp`](#naga-mcp) | Model Context Protocol server over stdio |
| [`naga assist`](#naga-assist) | one headless assistant turn |

## naga examples

```text
usage: naga examples [-h] [--path]

List the models that ship in the package. A command that takes a model path
also takes one of these names: naga run single_server.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --path      print the folder they are in instead
```

## naga run

```text
usage: naga run [-h] [--version] [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--seed SEED]
                [--warmup WARMUP] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH] [--start ISO]
                [--until ISO] [--timezone IANA] [--workers WORKERS]
                [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--export FORMAT:PATH]
                [--player PATH] [--state FILE] [--no-logs]
                model

Run a Naga model headless.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.replications'
  --seed SEED
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        0 = run until the queue drains; default: the model's
                        own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --start ISO           real instant model time 0 stands for, e.g.
                        2026-01-05T06:00:00 ; overrides the model's own
                        'simulation.calendar.start'
  --until ISO           run until this real instant instead of a length; needs
                        a calendar start, from the model or from --start
  --timezone IANA       IANA timezone for --start/--until and for weekday
                        schedules (default: the model's own, else UTC)
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes, or 'auto'
                        (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the 10-sheet results workbook here
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --export FORMAT:PATH  write with a registered exporter, e.g. json:out.json;
                        repeatable. See nagasim.exporters.EXPORTER_REGISTRY
                        for the built-in formats (xlsx/csv/html/json/player)
                        plus any plugin ones
  --player PATH         write a shareable HTML player of the first replication
                        here: one self-contained file that replays the run in
                        a browser, with no server (the same as --export
                        player:PATH)
  --state FILE          start from this state document (`naga state take` or
                        `observe`): the run's clock starts where the state was
                        taken and its statistics cover the run from there
  --no-logs             do not record the per-event entity/resource/store
                        logs: faster and much smaller on a long run, and every
                        summary statistic is unchanged -- only the three flat
                        log sheets come back empty
```

## naga scenarios

```text
usage: naga scenarios [-h] [--scenario SCENARIOS]
                      [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                      [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                      [--no-crn] [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--player PATH]
                      model

Run named scenarios headless and compare them.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --scenario SCENARIOS  scenario name to run (default: all); may repeat
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.replications'
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes, or 'auto'
                        (default: 1)
  --no-crn              disjoint seeds per scenario (Welch's interval) instead
                        of paired CRN
  --out OUT             write the comparison table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --player PATH         write a shareable HTML player here: the first
                        replication of every scenario, run again with its seed
                        and recorded, in one self-contained file with a
                        scenario switch
```

## naga fit

```text
usage: naga fit [-h] [--column COLUMN] [--top TOP] [--shift] [--json JSON]
                data

Fit candidate distributions to a data column.

positional arguments:
  data             CSV/TSV/TXT or XLSX file

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
```

## naga doe

```text
usage: naga doe [-h] --factor FACTORS --response RESPONSE
                [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--design DESIGN] [--no-crn]
                [--surrogate {linear,quadratic,auto}] [--dataset DATASET]
                model

Run a design of experiments over model parameters.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --factor FACTORS      a factor, as 'path=kind:low:high[:step]' or
                        'path=cat:a|b|c'. kind is float/int/cat. Several
                        comma-separated paths before the '=' are driven with
                        the same value. May repeat. Example:
                        'resources.Agents.capacity=int:3:6'
  --response RESPONSE   the KPI key to analyse, e.g. 'system/Avg Throughput
                        Time'
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        replications per design point (default: 5)
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the result table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --design DESIGN       full[:levels] (default full:2), lhs:<n>, or oat
  --no-crn              give each design point its own seed block instead of
                        CRN
  --surrogate {linear,quadratic,auto}
                        fit a response surface over the design; included in
                        --report as its own section
  --dataset DATASET     write one row per (design point, replication) here, as
                        factors + responses + seed (.csv, or .parquet if
                        available)
```

## naga optimize

```text
usage: naga optimize [-h] --factor FACTORS --response RESPONSE
                     [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                     [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                     [--out OUT] [--report REPORT] [--goal {min,max}]
                     [--budget BUDGET] [--constraint CONSTRAINTS]
                     [--method {auto,pattern,optuna}]
                     [--indifference INDIFFERENCE]
                     [--min-improvement MIN_IMPROVEMENT]
                     model

Search model parameters for the best KPI within a replication budget.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --factor FACTORS      a factor, as 'path=kind:low:high[:step]' or
                        'path=cat:a|b|c'. kind is float/int/cat. Several
                        comma-separated paths before the '=' are driven with
                        the same value. May repeat. Example:
                        'resources.Agents.capacity=int:3:6'
  --response RESPONSE   the KPI key to analyse, e.g. 'system/Avg Throughput
                        Time'
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        replications per design point (default: 5)
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the result table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --goal {min,max}
  --budget BUDGET       total replications the search may spend (default: 300)
  --constraint CONSTRAINTS
                        a KPI constraint, as '<kpi key><=<value>' or '<kpi
                        key>>=<value>'. May repeat. Example:
                        'resource/Agents/Usage % (snapshot)<=85'
  --method {auto,pattern,optuna}
  --indifference INDIFFERENCE
                        the smallest difference worth detecting in the final
                        ranking-and-selection step (default: 5% of the best
                        mean)
  --min-improvement MIN_IMPROVEMENT
                        relative gain a move must reach before the search
                        widens that factor's step (default: 0.01 = 1% of the
                        objective). 0 widens on any significant gain
```

## naga validate

```text
usage: naga validate [-h] [--json] model

Validate a model file and report structured problems (code, severity, path,
hint).

positional arguments:
  model       path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name (naga
              examples)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      emit the problems as a JSON array instead of one line each
```

## naga fmt

```text
usage: naga fmt [-h] [--check] files [files ...]

Rewrite model files in their shortest canonical form: every value the engine
fills in anyway left out, keys in one order, "$schema" first. The model, and
every run of it, stays the same.

positional arguments:
  files       model JSON files, rewritten in place

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --check     change nothing; name each file not in that form and exit 1
```

## naga export

```text
usage: naga export [-h] --python [-o OUT] model

Write a model as code that builds it again (nagasim.build). Running the code
gives the model in the form `naga fmt` writes.

positional arguments:
  model              path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name (naga
                     examples)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --python           Python code using nagasim.build (the one format so far)
  -o OUT, --out OUT  write the code here instead of printing it
```

## naga diff

```text
usage: naga diff [-h] [--json] [--all] [--textconv] files [files ...]

Semantic diff between two model files, matched by record identity rather than
list position.

positional arguments:
  files       two model files, or one with --textconv

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      emit the changes as a JSON array
  --all       also report canvas-only 'moved' changes (hidden by default)
  --textconv  print one file's canonical text form (a git textconv driver)
```

## naga merge

```text
usage: naga merge [-h] [-o OUTPUT] [--json] base ours theirs

Three-way merge of model files by record identity; usable as a git merge
driver (naga merge %%O %%A %%B).

positional arguments:
  base                  the common ancestor (git %O)
  ours                  our version (git %A); overwritten unless -o is given
  theirs                their version (git %B)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        write the merged model here instead of over OURS
  --json                also print the conflicts as a JSON array on stdout
```

## naga discover

```text
usage: naga discover [-h] [--check] [-o OUTPUT] [--report REPORT]
                     [--format {csv,xes}]
                     [--time-unit {seconds,minutes,hours,days}]
                     [--routing {auto,markov,variants}] [--case COLUMN]
                     [--activity COLUMN] [--timestamp COLUMN]
                     [--lifecycle COLUMN] [--resource COLUMN] [--start COLUMN]
                     [--complete COLUMN]
                     log

Draft a model from an event log (CSV, or XES): arrivals, activity times,
routing and resources as the log shows them, with a report of what was
inferred, assumed and dropped.

positional arguments:
  log                   the event log: a CSV file, an .xes file, or the name
                        of a bundled sample (job_shop_log)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --check               only check the log: what it holds and what that means
                        for a draft; no model is written
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        write the draft model here (default: stdout)
  --report REPORT       write the report as JSON here
  --format {csv,xes}    the log's format (default: by the file's suffix)
  --time-unit {seconds,minutes,hours,days}
                        the draft's time unit; a numeric timestamp is taken as
                        in it
  --routing {auto,markov,variants}
                        markov: chances to the next activity; variants: one
                        routing per observed sequence; auto picks by a test on
                        the log
  --case COLUMN         the CSV column holding the case (default: found by
                        name)
  --activity COLUMN     the CSV column holding the activity (default: found by
                        name)
  --timestamp COLUMN    the CSV column holding the timestamp (default: found
                        by name)
  --lifecycle COLUMN    the CSV column holding the lifecycle (default: found
                        by name)
  --resource COLUMN     the CSV column holding the resource (default: found by
                        name)
  --start COLUMN        the CSV column holding the start (default: found by
                        name)
  --complete COLUMN     the CSV column holding the complete (default: found by
                        name)
```

## naga viewer

```text
usage: naga viewer [-h] [-o OUTPUT] [--title TITLE] [--runtime DIR] [--fetch]
                   [--freeze] [--allow-network] [--allow-private-network]
                   [--allow-host HOST] [--connections FILE]
                   [model]

Write one HTML file in which the engine runs in a browser and re-runs the
model with the inputs its dashboard definition exposes. The file holds the
whole model and the engine's source: whoever receives it can read both. For a
confidential model share a recording instead (`naga run MODEL --player
FILE.html`).

positional arguments:
  model                 the model file, or a bundled model's name (naga
                        examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        the HTML file to write
  --title TITLE         the page's title (default: the model file's name)
  --runtime DIR         the folder of the browser runtime (default:
                        $NAGASIM_VIEWER_RUNTIME, else the user's own copy)
  --fetch               download the browser runtime (Pyodide 314.0.7, 29 MB,
                        from github.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net) into that
                        folder; nothing is downloaded without this flag
  --freeze              read the model's data sources once, now, and write the
                        values read into the copy as plain model data: the
                        file then names no source, path or address (without it
                        a model with data sources is refused)
  --allow-network       permit sql / json_url data sources (refused by
                        default: opening a model must not make outbound
                        connections on its own)
  --allow-private-network
                        also permit private/intranet addresses (refused even
                        with --allow-network)
  --allow-host HOST     restrict network sources to this hostname; may repeat
  --connections FILE    the connections a live source (rest, mqtt, opcua) may
                        name: a JSON file of yours, never the model's; without
                        it every live source is refused
```

## naga watch

```text
usage: naga watch [-h] --connections FILE [--source NAME] [--for SECONDS]
                  [--record FILE] [--check]
                  model

Print what a model's live data sources (rest, mqtt, opcua) send, as it
arrives, with a summary per source. Read-only: nothing is sent to a plant.

positional arguments:
  model               path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name (naga
                      examples)

options:
  -h, --help          show this help message and exit
  --connections FILE  your connections file: where each connection a source
                      names may connect, and with which credential
  --source NAME       watch only this source; may repeat (default: every live
                      source)
  --for SECONDS       how long to watch (default 30; 0: until Ctrl+C)
  --record FILE       also write every event as one JSON object per line, with
                      a {"lost": n} or {"gap": true} line where the log has a
                      hole
  --check             print each connection the model uses, connect once and
                      stop
```

## naga state

```text
usage: naga state [-h] {take,observe,check} ...

A model's state as a document: taken from a run, observed from a plant through
the model's data bindings, and checked before a run starts from it (naga run
MODEL --state FILE). Read-only.

positional arguments:
  {take,observe,check}
    take                run the model to a time and write its state
    observe             read the state a plant reports now, through the
                        model's bindings into initial_state
    check               say whether a run of this model may start from this
                        state; exit 1 with the reasons when not

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

## naga plant

```text
usage: naga plant [-h] {check,init,mock,replay,watch} ...

A plant as a timeline: a plant mapping (*.plantmap.json) says what each key a
plant sends asserts about a model, and the views of a run then show the plant.
Read-only: nothing is sent to a plant.

positional arguments:
  {check,init,mock,replay,watch}
    check               say whether a mapping may be used with a model; exit 1
                        with the reasons when not
    init                write a starter mapping that names every block,
                        resource and level of the model by its own name
    mock                run the model and write the plant log that run would
                        have left, through the mapping read backwards
    replay              map a recorded log (naga watch --record) into an
                        observed timeline
    watch               show a model's live sources as an observed timeline,
                        as they send

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

## naga twin

```text
usage: naga twin [-h] {once,run,status,score,reproduce} ...

An operational twin of a plant: monitor it through a plant mapping, forecast
from its state of now, compare each forecast with what then happened, score
them, and write one result a monitor reads. With --candidates it compares your
candidate actions after each forecast and recommends. Read-only towards the
plant: nothing is sent to it; only the --out directory is written and, with
--outbox, the file you name there.

positional arguments:
  {once,run,status,score,reproduce}
    once                one cycle with its forecast, for the OS scheduler;
                        exit 1 when the result holds an error
    run                 keep monitoring, with a forecast on its own slower
                        cadence, until Ctrl+C
    status              print the latest result of a twin; exit 1 for an error
                        in it or no result
    score               compute a twin's stored scores again from a recorded
                        plant log; exit 1 for any difference. Nothing is
                        written
    reproduce           compute a twin's stored recommendations again from
                        their stored states and seeds; exit 1 for any
                        difference. Nothing is written

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

## naga calibrate

```text
usage: naga calibrate [-h] --factor FACTORS --target TARGETS [--budget BUDGET]
                      [--replications REPLICATIONS] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH]
                      [--warmup WARMUP] [--seed SEED] [--workers WORKERS]
                      [--out OUT] [--report REPORT]
                      [--write-scenario WRITE_SCENARIO]
                      model

Tune model parameters until the model reproduces observed KPIs.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --factor FACTORS      a factor, as 'path=kind:low:high[:step]' or
                        'path=cat:a|b|c'. kind is float/int/cat. Several
                        comma-separated paths before the '=' are driven with
                        the same value. May repeat. Example:
                        'resources.Agents.capacity=int:3:6'
  --target TARGETS      an observed KPI, as '<kpi key>=<value>[:<tolerance>]'.
                        May repeat. Example: 'system/Avg Throughput
                        Time=8.4:0.5'
  --budget BUDGET       total replications the search may spend (default: 200)
  --replications REPLICATIONS
                        replications per candidate point (default: 5)
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        default: the model's own 'simulation.time_limit'
  --warmup WARMUP       default: the model's own 'simulation.warmup'
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --out OUT             write the target table here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
  --write-scenario WRITE_SCENARIO
                        write the model back here with the tuned values as a
                        scenario
```

## naga forecast

```text
usage: naga forecast [-h] --horizon HORIZON [--replications REPLICATIONS]
                     [--event EVENTS] [--kpi KPIS] [--seed SEED]
                     [--workers WORKERS] [--no-bind] [--allow-network]
                     [--allow-private-network] [--allow-host HOST]
                     [--connections FILE] [--out OUT] [--report REPORT]
                     model

Forecast a short horizon from the model's current state, with prediction bands
and event probabilities. Schedule repeated runs with the OS scheduler (Task
Scheduler, cron); this command is the unit of work, not a daemon.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --horizon HORIZON     run length in base time units
  --replications REPLICATIONS
  --event EVENTS        an event to report the probability of, as '<kpi
                        key><op><value>' with op one of > >= < <=. May repeat.
                        Example: 'timeseries/system/WIP/max>8'
  --kpi KPIS            KPI key to report; may repeat (default: all)
  --seed SEED
  --workers WORKERS     replications to run in parallel processes (default: 1)
  --no-bind             skip the model's data bindings (they resolve by
                        default here)
  --allow-network       permit sql / json_url data sources (refused by
                        default: opening a model must not make outbound
                        connections on its own)
  --allow-private-network
                        also permit private/intranet addresses (refused even
                        with --allow-network)
  --allow-host HOST     restrict network sources to this hostname; may repeat
  --connections FILE    the connections a live source (rest, mqtt, opcua) may
                        name: a JSON file of yours, never the model's; without
                        it every live source is refused
  --out OUT             write the forecast tables here (.xlsx or .csv)
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report here
```

## naga plan

```text
usage: naga plan [-h] [--orders ORDERS]
                 [--propose {makespan,weighted_tardiness}]
                 [--time-limit TIME_LIMIT] [--risk N] [--workers WORKERS]
                 [--seed SEED] [--export EXPORT] [--report REPORT]
                 model

What is the plan, is there a better one, and how risky is it -- the
deterministic schedule, an optional CP-SAT proposal, and optional risk.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --orders ORDERS       CSV replacing the model's "orders" section
  --propose {makespan,weighted_tardiness}
                        propose a plan with CP-SAT instead of the as-is layout
                        (needs the optional 'ortools' package: pip install
                        "nagasim[plan]")
  --time-limit TIME_LIMIT
                        CP-SAT time limit in seconds (default: 10)
  --risk N              score the plan with N stochastic replications
  --workers WORKERS     risk replications run in parallel
  --seed SEED
  --export EXPORT       write the plan here: .csv or .json by extension
  --report REPORT       write an HTML report (Gantt + risk table) here
```

## naga loops

```text
usage: naga loops [-h] [--seed SEED] [--run-length RUN_LENGTH] [--limit LIMIT]
                  [--csv FILE]
                  model

Loop dominance (Loops That Matter) of an SD model: which feedback loop drives
the behaviour and when. Needs simulation.sd.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model JSON, or a bundled model's name
                        (naga examples)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --seed SEED
  --run-length RUN_LENGTH
                        run length in base time units (default: the model's
                        own)
  --limit LIMIT         elementary circuits enumerated before the strongest-
                        path search takes over (default: 1000)
  --csv FILE            write the loop table to FILE and the per-step scores
                        to FILE's stem + '_dominance.csv'
```

## naga mcp

```text
usage: naga mcp [-h] [--root ROOT] [--allow-network] [--allow-private-network]
                [--allow-host HOST] [--connections FILE]
                [--tools {all,compact}] [--twin DIR]

Run the MCP server over stdio. File access is confined to --root, and network
access is off unless you allow it here.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --root ROOT           workspace root: the only directory models may be read
                        from or written to (default: the current directory)
  --allow-network       permit sql / json_url data sources (refused by
                        default: opening a model must not make outbound
                        connections on its own)
  --allow-private-network
                        also permit private/intranet addresses (refused even
                        with --allow-network)
  --allow-host HOST     restrict network sources to this hostname; may repeat
  --connections FILE    the connections a live source (rest, mqtt, opcua) may
                        name: a JSON file of yours, never the model's; without
                        it every live source is refused
  --tools {all,compact}
                        all: every tool (default); compact: only what
                        building, running and saving a model needs
                        (get_model_format, write_model, run_model, ...), so a
                        client pays for fewer tool descriptions
  --twin DIR            the result directory of a twin you started (naga twin
                        run --out DIR): two read-only tools then answer from
                        it. No tool can start a twin or choose this directory
```

## naga assist

```text
usage: naga assist [-h] [--provider {anthropic,openai}] [--base-url BASE_URL]
                   [--model-id MODEL_ID]
                   [--reasoning {none,low,medium,high,omit}]
                   [--max-tool-rounds MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS]
                   model prompt

Run one assistant turn against a model file, with a local model or your own
API key.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model .json file, or a bundled model's
                        name (naga examples)
  prompt                what to ask the assistant to do

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --provider {anthropic,openai}
                        anthropic, or openai for any OpenAI-compatible server
                        (Ollama, LM Studio); default: anthropic when
                        ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else a local Ollama
  --base-url BASE_URL   default http://localhost:11434/v1
  --model-id MODEL_ID   the provider's model name (for Ollama, one from
                        `ollama list`)
  --reasoning {none,low,medium,high,omit}
  --max-tool-rounds MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS
```
